•	Vanilla Matcha Latte

featured_reviews.name: Soumitra Sinha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Six of us walked into Grounded Cafe this morning after a nice Sunday morning long drive. Pretty hungry of course. Very chilled out ambience. A real cafe atmosphere. The food orders were varied --- from a full English breakfast, Eggs Florentine to Pancakes and Crepe; coffees and an Orange flavoured hot chocolate.  Great tasting fresh food served with a smile. The hash browns as a side needs a special mention....just the right crisp with a yummy inside. We were so happily full that a single portion of Nutella Tiramisu was ordered for us to share. Don't miss this desert as the cup and cover are made of Nutella.
Now folks, that is what I call an amazing Sunday breakfast.
Great place. Great food. Great ambience.😃

Hi Soumitra,
What a delightful way to spend a Sunday morning! It's wonderful to hear that you and your friends enjoyed everything from the full English breakfast to the Nutella Tiramisu. The mention of our crispy hash browns makes us smile, as we love taking the time to perfect our dishes. Your description of the relaxed atmosphere truly captures the essence of what we aim for at Grounded Cafe.
Thank you,
Team Grounded

featured_reviews.review_text:

The café also allows you to bring in your own pets.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:

Thank you for taking the time to share your experience. It's wonderful to hear that you found our café to be a peaceful spot, perfect for enjoying our coffee and delicious croissants. We appreciate your input regarding the chocolate drink and will ensure our team is reminded to provide the best flavors consistently.
Thank you,
Team Grounded

featured_reviews.name: Dinesh Katke
featured_reviews.review_text: If you’re wandering around Bandstand in Bandra and looking for a cozy spot to refuel, Grounded is a fantastic choice. The overall ambience is incredibly pleasant, making it a perfect escape from the hustle and bustle of the promenade. The highlight of my visit was easily the Callebaut Hot Chocolate with whipped cream. It was absolutely delicious rich, velvety, and honestly one of the best hot chocolates I’ve ever had. To balance the indulgence, I tried the Healthy Chicken Ragi Wrap. It’s rare to find something that feels both nutritious and genuinely tasty, but this wrap nailed it. The staff also deserves a special shoutout; they were super polite, kind, and made the experience feel very welcoming. The only minor drawback was the music volume. It was a little loud for my taste, which made conversation a bit tricky at times. However, that’s a negligible part of an otherwise awesome experience. Between the quality of the food and the kindness of the team, I’ll definitely be back.

Your delightful description of our Callebaut Hot Chocolate and the Healthy Chicken Ragi Wrap brightens our day! It’s wonderful to hear that you enjoyed the cozy atmosphere and experienced such attentive service. We’re always looking to create a pleasant haven away from the busy promenade in Bandra. We'll certainly look into the music volume to enhance the conversation experience for our guests. Looking forward to welcoming you back soon!
Thank you,
Team Grounded

featured_reviews.name: Nalini
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had brunch here for the first time after hearing about it from colleagues. I ordered the Truffle cheddar scrambled eggs and a black tea .
The scrambled eggs were delicious and served with a salad and sourdough bread . Excellent combination. The tea was Twinings so a clear focus on quality.
Here is where I was disappointed ..the music at first was way too loud to finish my work, let alone think but a lady called Jhanvi very sweetly noticed and lowered the volume.
Also in attendance were a couple of flies (unnecessary desi touch ) and my eggs were served in a chipped plate.

However, on the positive side, Ebrahim and Imam were warm and friendly , served my food , asked how it tasted  and kindly returned my sunglasses I left behind . It didn’t feel forced .

Afterwards I spoke to Jhanvi ,the sweet smiley lady who rescued me from going deaf and turns out she is in charge of Marketing. She was most responsive to my feedback .

I wish this beautiful located Cafe the best of luck and hope they do well enough to lower the prices a tad . For my eggs and tea I paid Rs 736, of which Rs 96 was service charge + taxes. Left a rather small cash tip as I paid a 10% service charge .

Speaking of which , they lost electricity just when it came to swiping my credit card so I paid in cash.
All in all a cute pricey place with a menu that’s trendy .
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Nalini,
It's wonderful to hear you enjoyed the Truffle cheddar scrambled eggs and appreciated the quality of the Twinings tea. Your feedback about the music and the flies is invaluable, and I’m glad Jhanvi could assist in creating a more comfortable environment for you. We’re addressing the issue with the chipped plate to ensure the presentation of our dishes matches their quality. Thank you for your kind wishes; we’ll continue working to enhance your experience.
Thank you,
Team Grounded

featured_reviews.name: Ashok Sankaran
featured_reviews.review_text: This tiny cafe on Waterfield Road is perfect for dinner with you and your family. The cozy setting, featuring pale green and pink decorations, gives you that perfect peaceful atmosphere. Earth Cafe offers a variety of options whether you’re vegetarian, Jain or just wanting something different. The food is high quality with something for everyone. The avocado bruschetta has the perfect amount of crispness and flavour. The fries are freshly made, perfect for a crunchy starter. The peach and mint mojito is to die for. To choose a main dish is nearly impossible. From freshly baked sourdough pizzas or piping hot risotto. The lasagna is an amazing dish with layered zucchini and a creamy vegan sauce. If you’re not already stuffed and want a sweet treat, they have a variety of cakes to choose from including some gluten free options. But the perfect treat for summer is the mango and cream. The service was exceptional and the staff were super helpful. Overall an amazing place to dine out. Rahul who served us during our visit was great.

featured_reviews.name: Niyati Singhvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re tired of the long wait times at Boojee Cafe, walk a few metres over to Bokka Coffee.
Honestly, the quality is just as competitive without the headache. We were a group of two and got seated immediately (luckily enough). The staff was incredibly responsive and attentive to us. I highly recommend the chocolate bowl if you want something indulgent, and the hibiscus iced tea is perfect for something refreshing.
It’s not "cheap," but it certainly won't burn a hole in your pocket—it’s priced just right for the experience.
Plus, the plant-filled, well-lit decor makes for a great atmosphere.
Definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Suhel Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Heard this is one of Shahid Kapoor’s favorite coffee spots, so decided to drop by and give it a try. Located in the busy lanes of Khar, the café thankfully offers valet parking, which is a big plus.

The space is cozy but quite compact, so some wait time is expected during rush hours. Seating can feel a bit close together, and note that laptops or tablets aren’t allowed, so it’s not a spot to work from. The ambiance is warm and inviting, filled with plants and soft lighting that adds to the charm.

Service was excellent — staff were attentive and quick to respond. Tried the iced Americano, which had a nice balance of flavor without being overly bitter. The Harvest Salad with salmon was fresh and generous in portion, and the Berry Bowl was naturally sweet with no added sugar.

Pricing is on par with other popular cafés in the area.

featured_reviews.review_text:
you're ever around Pali Hill, Bandra West, and looking for a cozy, aesthetic spot to chill with friends or even get some work done, Ritual Daily Coffee should definitely be on your list. This café is not only known for its specialty coffee but also for its calm ambience, comfortable seating, and work-friendly vibe.

We tried their Iced Vanilla Latte, and it was as good as it looked — smooth, refreshing, and perfectly balanced in flavor. My friend went for the Biscoff Frappe, and honestly, it was a game-changer. The taste was unique and indulgent, with that Biscoff twist hitting all the right notes.

Now, let's talk food — we ordered their Rose Chicken Croffle Sandwich, and wow, this was mind-blowing. The flavor, the creativity, the texture — everything about it stood out. I can confidently say you won’t find a sandwich like this anywhere else in Mumbai. My friend and I both absolutely loved it.

We also tried the Chicken Club Sandwich, and it was packed with juicy chicken and fresh vegetables — hearty, flavorful, and satisfying. The Chicken Cilantro Quesadillas were another highlight, highly recommended by the staff, and they didn’t disappoint.

The cherry on top? Their Mango Basque Cheesecake. Soft, rich, and just the right amount of sweet — it was the perfect way to end our meal.

Service was excellent, with the staff being super friendly and helpful in recommending their best dishes. The overall experience was a solid 10/10.

Whether you're looking for a new coffee hangout, a place to work, or just craving some standout food, Ritual Daily Coffee is definitely worth the visit.

featured_reviews.name: Tanishka Rajpal
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a warm and cozy café in Bandra West, Rituals Café is such a lovely find! From the moment you walk in, the vibe feels inviting – it has that cute, aesthetic charm that makes you want to sit down, relax, and just spend hours there. The upper deck seating is one of my favorite parts – perfect for catching up with friends, getting some work done, or even just enjoying a quiet coffee by yourself.

Coming to the food – I tried their mac & cheese and it was exactly what comfort food should taste like: creamy, cheesy, and super satisfying. The avo toast with burrata was fresh and delicious, such a perfect combination. For dessert, I went with their gluten-free chocolate cake and honestly, I couldn’t believe it was gluten-free – it was rich, fudgy, and just the right amount of sweetness. I also loved their 54% sugar-free Belgian chocolate – guilt-free but still indulgent. To finish, I had the Brazilian blueberry smoothie, which was refreshing, light, and packed with flavor.

What I really like is that everything feels thoughtfully made, and the presentation is just as good as the taste. It’s not just a café, but a spot where you can actually unwind and feel good while enjoying great food. Definitely one of those hidden gems in Bandra that I’ll be revisiting for sure. Highly recommend to anyone who loves cozy corners, comfort food, and cute café vibes! 💛

I went to this spot on Saturday morning for breakfast, and it turned out to be a fantastic experience for us.

We ordered one Cortado, a large Pain au Chocolat, a spicy chicken-stuffed hash brown, an avocado chicken sandwich, and a Caramel Latte.

The cortado was incredible; it's a traditional Spanish espresso drink made with double espresso and 60 ml of milk. It had a bitter flavour, but I really enjoyed it.

The large pain au chocolat was absolutely delicious, a classic pastry crafted from buttery, flaky, laminated dough (similar to croissant dough) wrapped around dark chocolate sticks.

The spicy chicken-stuffed hash brown was tasty, featuring shredded potatoes filled with cooked chicken, pan-fried until golden and crispy.The avocado chicken sandwich was mouthwatering and highly recommended. The caramel latte was incredibly refreshing. It’s a sweet and creamy coffee drink typically made with espresso, steamed milk, and caramel syrup.

Personally, I didn’t enjoy it as much, but it definitely feels like an acquired taste, so cold brew enthusiasts should still give it a shot.

Overall, a really nice cafe with great vibes, good food and excellent coffee. Would definitely recommend checking it out if you’re in and around Bandra.

The ground floor has a bakery-style setup with a display of baked sweets and goodies. I didn’t try anything from there, but it does add a warm, inviting feel the moment you enter.

The first floor, accessed via quite steep stairs, is an enclosed, air-conditioned space with enough room for group meetups. It feels more structured and social. I chose to sit on the second floor, which is an open seating area and easily the highlight of the cafe. There’s a shared seating arrangement with long tables along the edges, facing outward, so you’re not directly facing other people. For introverts, this layout is a blessing. What truly stands out is the massive old banyan tree around 100-150 years old running through the cafe. Instead of cutting it down, the cafe has been built around it, which adds a calm, grounding presence to the space.
The ambience on the second floor is peaceful and airy, perfect for reading a book, journaling, or simply sitting and observing the surroundings. Since the cafe is tucked away in a small gully within a residential area, there’s minimal noise and a very relaxed atmosphere.

Service was quick, with food arriving within 10-15 minutes each time. The server, Sarah, was especially friendly and easy to talk to, which made the experience even more pleasant. Overall, the cafe balances good food, thoughtful design, and quiet comfort very well.

Visited Grey Soul Coffee Roasters in Bandra to explore their pour-over program, and it’s clear the café is serious about specialty coffee. The menu is thoughtfully structured, with detailed coffee cards covering estate, varietal, altitude, and processing.

I tried the “Raspberry in Loop” from Zoya Estate (Chikmagalur), a light roast featuring S795 and Chandragiri varietals processed through multi-stage anaerobic fermentation. On paper, this is a high-potential coffee designed for a fruit-forward, layered profile.

In the cup, however, the experience didn’t fully align with expectations. While the coffee was clean and free of defects, the flavor expression felt muted — the brighter fruit notes (pineapple, mandarin, raspberry) and deeper chocolate tones were not clearly defined. The cup leaned more toward a subdued, flattened profile rather than the vibrant complexity suggested by the processing.

The barista interaction was informative and helpful, and the overall setup reflects a strong intent toward quality and transparency.

Grey Soul is still worth visiting for those interested in Indian specialty coffee and experimental processing. However, in this instance, the brewing didn’t fully unlock the potential of an otherwise very interesting coffee.

Bandstand Pantry is one of those cafés that remains popular for good reason. Located right by Bandstand, it works especially well for a relaxed breakfast, a solo meal, or an easy outing with family.

The menu has enough variety to suit different moods and appetites — from smoothies, smoothie bowls, sandwiches, and salads to more comforting options like mac and cheese and mushroom pâté. They also have a good selection of egg dishes and teas & coffees (hot or cold). My kids especially enjoy the mac and cheese, the chicken mushroom pâté, and the hot chocolate, while I keep going back for the lemon mint iced tea. Their avocado-on-toast options are also worth mentioning, especially because they offer a smaller portion size — something I genuinely appreciate when dining alone.

Because the café has open seating on the main road, evenings can get noisy. Breakfast, however, is a very different experience — calmer, with a sea view and the sound of the waves in the background. The strong fans and sea breeze also make the outdoor seating more comfortable than you might expect.

What stands out most to me is the attention to hygiene and service. Tables are cleared and cleaned quickly, and the staff is alert and efficient. I have also noticed them actively keeping crows away in the mornings so guests can eat in peace — a small but very real detail in this location.

A special mention for the staff member who usually greets guests at the entrance. He is warm, quick to help with seating, and knows the menu well enough to make thoughtful recommendations.

For a meal for two, the pricing feels reasonable for the area. It is also pet-friendly, which adds to its appeal. Overall, Bandstand Pantry is a dependable option when you want a comfortable café meal in Bandra, especially if you are looking for something that works well before or after a walk or workout at Bandstand.

Visited this Delhi and Mumbai's famous coffee cafe in Bandra at by lane of Pali hill. Such a cosy place to unwind with great coffee and food.

Hot Brews:

•	Peppermint Mocha- This had peppermint dark chocolate nibs of Mason & Co which perfectly gave the minty taste with strong coffee flavour.

Food-
•	Almond Croissant: This is the best croissant I’ve ever had in my life. Very buttery, soft, sweet with amazing sugary fillings and sprinkled with almonds on top. Just loved it!
•	New York style Bagel: These are soft and chewy bagels served with sesame with crunchier crust. Yum
•	Soft Bagel: It is the basic bagel served with sesame; these are soft, not so chewy bagels with a crunch.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Tuskin Coffee is one of those places that instantly hooks you. I love the bright blue & theme, and simple vibe.

The prices are super reasonable for how good the coffee is, which already feels like a win. Compared to the insanely overpriced Starbucks next door, they serve great tasting coffee, way better than SB.

The oat milk added this really smooth, balanced bitter-sweet vibe that just worked.

I also grabbed a cinnamon roll. Bhavin, The barista warmed it up in the oven and it came out perfectly flaky, soft, and melt-in-your-mouth good. Honestly dangerous.

The biggest compliment I can give? I loved it so much I went back three days in a row. You can really tell they source quality coffee beans because it shines through in every drink. I’m already eyeing the Arena and the Tuskin Latte for my next visits.

Safe to say they’ve got a customer for life.

Light, flavorful, and perfectly cooked, it felt like one of those special dishes you remember long after the meal is over.

Incredible food, heartfelt service, and an atmosphere that makes you want to linger. We loved every minute and can’t wait to return.

She then went to check with the kitchen and came back saying they could make a vegetarian version — BUT if “anything goes wrong,” they would not take it back and we would still have to eat it.

Seriously? Who speaks to customers like that? What kind of hospitality is this? Why would anyone say something so bizarre to hungry guests trying to place an order?

Then another male waiter came in and confidently said he “guarantees” it would be made properly and that we should order it. At that point it honestly felt like some strange game was being played with us.

Since we were already hungry, we went ahead and ordered a Paneer Shawarma and a Paneer Shashlik Sizzler.

The Paneer Shawarma was unbearably salty. When the waiter came to ask for feedback, we politely mentioned it was far too salty. His response? A smile followed by: “Idhar aisa hi banta hai.”

Unbelievable.

Then came the sizzler. While it was generally edible, two pieces of paneer were clearly stale. When we informed the staff, they simply ignored the issue and picked up the plate without apology, concern, or even acknowledgment.

Poor food, terrible attitude, zero accountability, and absolutely no customer service. Definitely not a place we would recommend or revisit.

We recently visited Aromas Café & Bistro, located at Ground Floor, Mamta Building, Waterfield Road, Linking Road, near National College, Bandra West, Mumbai, and had a wonderful experience.

The ambience is extremely cozy and inviting, with well-designed interiors that make it a perfect place to relax. featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Slow in Kandivli recently with my cousin sister, and honestly, while the food and coffee were good, the overall experience and service left us extremely uncomfortable.

When we entered, there were multiple empty 4-seater tables available (which remained empty throughout most of our visit), yet we were seated at their “community table”  which is essentially a tiny circular table against the wall that is genuinely not practical for two people ordering food and drinks.

One of the waiters later moved us to a proper table after realizing the issue, but shortly after, someone managing the cafe asked the waiter to move us back to the tiny community table again. We even mentioned that it would be difficult to comfortably eat there once food arrived, but were told “it will be fine.”

Unfortunately, it really wasn’t.

Things kept falling while we were eating because there simply wasn’t enough space. We had to move the cutlery setup ourselves just to make room for the plates and drinks. Nobody checked in or offered any solution despite clearly seeing the inconvenience.

What honestly made the experience worse was noticing another individual sitting alone with camera equipment/content setup being comfortably given a larger table while we, as paying customers ordering food and coffee, were repeatedly denied one despite tables remaining vacant throughout our meal.

If the cafe had been full, this would’ve been understandable. But it wasn’t.

The food itself was genuinely good and reasonably priced, which makes this more disappointing because the experience could have been great with just basic consideration and hospitality.

Also adding a service charge after this experience honestly felt a little absurd.

I hope the cafe improves how they treat regular customers moving forward because good food alone isn’t enough to make people return.

featured_reviews.review_text: This café is a hidden gem with cosy vibes and a welcoming atmosphere. Pairing it with a Vietnamese iced latte was a delightful choice, and the tiramisu French toast was indulgent yet balanced. featured_reviews.name: Pragya Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
TLDR: Good ambience, (at best) average Food, terrible beverages. Overpriced disappointment!

We were genuinely excited to visit the place and had already returned twice because of the waiting earlier but God were we disappointed! Biggest let down was the signature cold chocolate which was just a sugary syrup and a disgrace to be called 55% dark chocolate. It tasted like drinking sweet flour (probably to make it thicker). Felt so bad about the extra calories and 400 bucks going down the drain for this whereas a small sachet of Tiggle does a WAYYY better job at home. I even requested the server if I could get a stronger version of chocolate by tweaking it after having just one sip but he refused by saying that the jaggery/palm sugar already comes mixed with the chocolate so there's nothing they can do about it.
The burrito bowl was average, not bad but nothing I'd go again for. And the nachos were a bit stale, so much for "fresh and from scratch" ingredients.
The broccoli and cottage cheese burger didn't feel like it had any cottage cheese but rather just broccoli and mushed potatoes. The hand cut fries that came with it were too salty, oily and soggy.
Lastly, the spiced orange cream iced latte only sounded fancy and had cream chunks instead of a well frothed foam on top.
The only good parts were that the ambience has been tastefully decorated and the service is quick.

The vegetarian menu focuses on wholesome comfort food, artisan coffees (including signature jaggery and salted caramel hot chocolate), and vegan options.

It is an aesthetic cafe indeed with great service and amazing food. Must visit if you are in Mumbai.
